geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the generic bend with a section-aware hall profile to better support neighborhood mixed-use and a legible roof/section.
Introduce a continuous folded section so the mass can carry a clearer public/upper hierarchy.
Keep the long-axis organization aligned with the bar gesture and frontage condition.
Add a carved public void without deleting the dominant mass so the ground plane becomes legible.
Size the void to read as a usable court rather than a shallow notch.
Orient the public opening to the verified access side in the program frame.
Make the public void the organizing root so the hall remains in its ancestry while the threshold becomes primary.

graph_edits.rationale: Keep the dominant bar anchor but make it more responsive to the access edge by changing the primary operator to a void-capable massing form.
Preserve the strong longitudinal gesture while preparing for a frontage-aligned void.
Add a public court to produce a legible ground threshold and strengthen the mixed-use street edge.
Size the court so it reads as usable public space rather than a decorative subtraction.
Align the public opening to the verified access side in the program frame.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent compact bar with a consistent stepped/curved top across views, so the overall mass is legible and repairable. However, it remains too sealed and object-like for the neighborhood living brief: the verified access edge is answered weakly, with little evidence of a public threshold, court, notch, or ground-level opening. The visible section does not yet convey an active street-facing base or a clear public void, so the building feels more like a compact stacked object than a mixed-use neighborhood edge condition. The silhouette is acceptable but not especially resolved as a capacity-bearing section; the dominant gesture is readable, yet the program relation is underdeveloped.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller and more tower-like than this candidate; do not copy the skyline object, only the clear layered mass logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stacked massing can express mixed-use hierarchy while keeping a strong base-to-top reading.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Restaurant/café scale and courtyard intimacy are stronger than the candidate; the building form itself is not a direct match.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A carved internal court and porous ground threshold can make a compact mass feel public and inhabitable.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is more landscape-forward and less tectonic; use the public void principle, not the material language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A sheltered open-to-sky void and softened edges can support neighborhood gathering and active ground space.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is a much larger tower condition; its vertical scale and complexity exceed the candidate.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A strong podium-and-upper-body hierarchy can support a mixed-use street building.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual and typologically off for this brief; useful only as a spatial operation cue, not as a form precedent.
